facts.label: Published benchmark: Share of single-family rental parcels owned by large corporate investors (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (city))
facts.vintage: published, read 2026-11-22
facts.note: Cited, not computed here. Large corporate investors are business entities owning 26 or more parcels in Philadelphia. The same owners hold about 2.5 percent of all single-family parcels. With a 100-or-more threshold the share would be about 7.0 percent. Source: Lei Ding, Sisi Zhang and Mckenzie Diep, "Ownership Profile of Single-Family Residence Properties in Philadelphia: A Focus on Large Corporate Investors", Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia, February 2025, Page 1 summary and page 3, Finding 1 (Figure 2); footnote 2. https://www.philadelphiafed.org/community-development/housing-and-neighborhoods/ownership-profile-of-single-family-residence-properties-in-philadelphia-large-corporate-investors

facts.label: Published benchmark: Share of arm's-length single-family home sales bought by investors and corporations (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (city))
facts.vintage: published, read 2026-11-22
facts.note: Cited, not computed here. Buyers whose names include words such as LLC or realty, or a property address, and individuals who bought more than two homes. Individual cash buyers are not counted, so the report calls this a floor; the yearly share ranged from 28 to 36 percent after 2002. Source: Octavia Howell, "Single-Family Home Sales in Philadelphia: What 20 years of city records tell us about how the market has changed", The Pew Charitable Trusts, July 2024, Overview, page 1; 'Types of homebuyers', page 5. https://www.pew.org/en/research-and-analysis/reports/2024/07/single-family-home-sales-in-philadelphia

sections.limits: An entity is not the same as an institutional investor: it includes one-home landlord companies, nonprofits, churches, banks after foreclosure and trusts, and many trusts are family estate planning. A missing homestead exemption does not prove a home is rented. Out-of-state means the tax bill goes outside Pennsylvania. Philadelphia's entity test reads owner and grantee names for words such as LLC and TRUST on the City's server; names are never kept. Deeds count arm's-length sales of homes that are single-family today. The published benchmarks use other definitions (for example owners of 26 or more homes) and are shown only for context. The City's data licence is to be confirmed; only totals are shown.

Taken from the Assumption Ledger, not state data: Share of residential land zoned for single-family homes only; Share of lots where an ADU is already allowed; Share of lots with room for a detached ADU (needs parcels); Development and impact fees per unit; Parking spaces required per unit.

acs5_summary_file.name: American Community Survey 5-year table-based summary files (2020-2024)
acs5_summary_file.limits: Estimates are survey averages over five years with margins of error; small tracts often have wide margins. One national pipe-delimited file per table (about 48 MB for B25024). Negative values are missing-value codes, not data.

fhfa_hpi_county.name: FHFA House Price Index, annual, counties
fhfa_hpi_county.limits: Repeat-sales index built from mortgages bought or guaranteed by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac; thin in rural counties, where years can be missing. Published as a spreadsheet (read with the standard library's zip and XML tools).

bps_county_annual.name: Building Permits Survey, county annual files
bps_county_annual.vintage: 1990-2025 annual files (the 2025 file is the latest published)
bps_county_annual.limits: Counts units authorized by permit, not units started or finished. Some counties are imputed rather than reported; the file flags which. Places without permit offices are not covered.

phl_li_permits.name: Philadelphia Licenses and Inspections building permits (permits)
phl_li_permits.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Department of Licenses and Inspections (via OpenDataPhilly, Carto SQL)
phl_li_permits.vintage: Permits as read on the build date, issued from 2016
phl_li_permits.limits: Permits issued, not homes started or finished. A record-system change in 2020 renamed permit types; both names are counted. A 2021 rush ahead of a tax abatement change inflates that year.

phfa_lihtc_awards.name: PHFA Low-Income Housing Tax Credit award lists
phfa_lihtc_awards.vintage: Award lists posted on the build date (from 2019; scanned lists are skipped)
phfa_lihtc_awards.limits: Awards, not homes built: some awarded projects are delayed or dropped. Read from PDFs whose layout changes yearly; a list with no text layer is skipped. Sites described as intersections or scattered sites have no tract.

pa_dced_munstats.name: Municipal Statistics, County / Municipal Planning, Zoning & Building Code report
pa_dced_munstats.publisher: Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development (DCED)
pa_dced_munstats.vintage: current (the report is kept up to date by DCED)
pa_dced_munstats.limits: Self-reported by municipalities and updated when they tell DCED; some entries may be out of date. Says whether an ordinance or plan exists, not what it allows or when it was last revised. DCED ids are matched to Census county subdivisions by name; unmatched names are listed in the build notes.

county_comprehensive_plans.name: County comprehensive plans (citation list in assumptions/plans.yaml)
county_comprehensive_plans.limits: A citation list for large counties only; each county's own page is the authority.

ntm_stops.name: National Transit Map, stops
ntm_stops.publisher: U.S. Department of Transportation, Bureau of Transportation Statistics
ntm_stops.vintage: National Transportation Atlas Database release compiled 2026-09-23
ntm_stops.limits: Stops as reported by agencies in their schedule feeds; some agencies are missing or out of date. Gives stop locations, not service frequency (frequency comes from the agency schedule feeds). About 673,000 stops nationally; queried by state bounding box in pages of at most 2,000.

tiger_2020_tabblock.name: TIGER/Line 2020 tabulation blocks (attribute table only)
tiger_2020_tabblock.limits: Housing units and population are 2020 counts, not current. Internal points are a point inside each block, not its centre of population. Only the attribute table (the .dbf, about 46 MB of the 409 MB Pennsylvania zip) is read, by HTTP range requests; block shapes are never downloaded.

phl_opa_properties.name: Philadelphia Properties and Assessment History (opa_properties_public)
phl_opa_properties.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Office of Property Assessment (via OpenDataPhilly, Carto SQL)
phl_opa_properties.vintage: Assessment file as read on the build date (tax year 2027 values at the time of writing)
phl_opa_properties.limits: Assessment records, not a census of who lives where. Market values are the City's mass-appraisal estimates. The last sale is the only sale on file, so repeat sales in a window are undercounted. Condominium units are filed as single family and are separated by building description.

phl_rtt_summary.name: Philadelphia Real Estate Transfers (rtt_summary)
phl_rtt_summary.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Department of Records (via OpenDataPhilly, Carto SQL)
phl_rtt_summary.vintage: Transfer records as read on the build date
phl_rtt_summary.limits: Grantee names are judged entity or person by word list only. The single-family test uses today's property category, not the category on the sale date.

philly_fed_owners_2025.name: Ownership Profile of Single-Family Residence Properties in Philadelphia: A Focus on Large Corporate Investors (cited benchmark, not ingested)
philly_fed_owners_2025.limits: Philadelphia only. Large corporate investors are entities with 26 or more parcels; the share is of single-family rentals, not all homes.

pew_phl_home_sales_2024.name: Single-Family Home Sales in Philadelphia (cited benchmark, not ingested)
pew_phl_home_sales_2024.limits: Philadelphia only. Investors include named entities and individuals buying more than two homes; cash buyers are not counted, so it is a floor.

cb_2020_tract.name: Cartographic boundary file, census tracts, 2020, 1:500,000
cb_2020_tract.limits: Generalized (simplified) shapes for maps, not for measuring land area or for parcel work. 2020 tracts match the 2020-2024 ACS.

gtfs_agency_feeds.name: Transit agency schedule feeds (GTFS), via their published addresses or the catalog mirror
gtfs_agency_feeds.publisher: Each transit agency (copies mirrored by MobilityData)
gtfs_agency_feeds.vintage: The schedule current when fetched; the representative date is recorded per feed
gtfs_agency_feeds.limits: Scheduled, not actual, service. One representative weekday per feed. Only feeds that download without a key are used; bus stops of other agencies are marked frequency unknown. Agencies change stop ids between schedules, so a few stops may not match the National Transit Map.

freddie_pmms.name: Primary Mortgage Market Survey, weekly rate history
freddie_pmms.limits: National average offered rates for prime borrowers, not the rate a given household or builder pays. The value used in the model is a ledger parameter with a range.

bls_qcew_construction.name: Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages, annual averages, construction (NAICS 23)
bls_qcew_construction.limits: Average pay of construction jobs at private employers, by where the employer reports, not where it builds. A wage index is a proxy for local building costs; materials, land and fees are not in it. BLS withholds county figures that would reveal one employer; those counties take the state value.
